cross_format.role: JSON holds data definitions (token tables, keyword lists). TOML holds configuration. If it's WHAT something is, JSON. If it's HOW something behaves, TOML.
cross_format.note: No direct TOML counterpart — generic data is JSON-native. TOML specs (types, composition) define structure; JSON data files carry instances.
cross_format.relationship: JSON generic data template derives from TOML root for pure data expression. TOML defines type structure; JSON carries type instances.

_Cc_format_note: JSON strict — no comments, no trailing commas, UTF-8, LF line endings.
_Cc_key_convention: lowercase_with_underscores for data keys, _prefix for documentation fields
_Cc_schema_pattern: _schema keys document expected types inline — the template teaches by being complete
_Co_note: Data values organized by purpose. Real content replaces this section on instantiation.
_Cv_expected_state: Valid JSON with all pragma, metadata, content, and closing blocks present.

_Cv_issues.parse_error: No trailing commas, check quotes, bracket matching
_Cv_issues.type_mismatch: Verify Go struct tags match JSON keys
